open loop vs closed loop system
html:
10 Open Loop Control System Examples and Their Closed Loop Versions

Most open loop control system examples become closed loop once a sensor and feedback are added. This table shows the difference between open loop and closed loop system versions of the same everyday and plant equipment.

Open loop exampleWhy it is open loopClosed loop version
Electric toasterTimer only, bread colour not measuredToaster with browning sensor
Washing machine timerRuns for fixed time, cleanliness not checkedMachine with turbidity sensor
Traffic light with fixed timerIgnores actual trafficTraffic light with vehicle detectors
Electric fan regulatorSpeed set by knob, room temperature ignoredFan with temperature control
Immersion water heaterHeats until switched offGeyser with thermostat
Manual control valveFixed opening, flow not measuredFlow control loop with PID
Stepper motor driveSteps counted, position not measuredServo motor with encoder
Rice cooker timerTime based cookingCooker with temperature sensor
Irrigation sprinkler timerIgnores soil moistureSprinkler with soil moisture sensor
Cloth dryer with timerFixed drying timeDryer with humidity sensor

In short, the open loop vs closed loop system choice depends on whether you can tolerate output error. Where disturbances change the result, use closed loop control.
